scripts.title_ja: Medusa wasn't always cursed（呪われたのではなかった）
scripts.text: In the best-known story, Medusa is cursed. But in one of the oldest accounts, Hesiod's Theogony, from around 700 BCE, there is no curse at all. Medusa is simply born a Gorgon, the only mortal one of three sisters.

scripts.title_ja: A monster's face as a guardian（怪物の顔が守り手に）
scripts.text: Why put a monster's face on a roof? In ancient Greece, Gorgon faces appeared on roof tiles, drinking cups, and shields. Many scholars think they were meant to scare away harm. The monster became a guardian.

scripts.title_ja: The beautiful Medusa（美しいメドゥーサ）
scripts.text: In art, Medusa was not always a monster. On this vase, painted in Athens around 450 BCE, she sleeps with a young, calm face. The Met describes it as one of the earliest images of Medusa as a beautiful young woman.
